messages.subject: what is the best way to run code paralel?
messages.subject_clean: what is the best way to run code paralel?
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

I need your advice on running code parallel. It seems there are many options out there, so I am wondering if anyone has a good practice.
I have one Rnw file in which some chunks need to be run one after another, but there is a great portion of code which can be run parallel (two different models). Computations are very intensive, that is why I want to  do it simultaneously and to use more than one core on my machine. I am not really eager to re-programme my code in order to use R packages that can do it for me.

I was more thinking of running two R instances on one Rnw file or using input chunks, I know you can do it with Vim R plugin. Or something similar.
At the end I want to collect my results back in one document.

I hope I managed to explain my intentions and looking forward to hear your thoughts.

Many thanks,
Olga

messages.subject: Re: what is the best way to run code paralel?
messages.subject_clean: what is the best way to run code paralel?
messages.body_plain:
I've never run R code in parallel before, but the rnoweb file below works for me:

\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{times}
\begin{document}

<<loadlibs>>=
library(multicore)
library(texreg)
@

<<genData>>=
y <- rnorm(100000)
w <- rnorm(100000) - 0.1 * y
x <- rnorm(100000) + 0.1 * y
@

<<printRegs, results="asis">>=
m1 <- parallel(lm(y ~ x))
m2 <- parallel(lm(y ~ w))
texreg(list(collect(m1)[[1]], collect(m2)[[1]]))
@

\end{document}

messages.body_plain:
The package multicore was incorporated into parallel package. So the example becomes:

\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{times}
\begin{document}

<<loadlib>>=
library(parallel)

library(texreg)
@

<<genData>>=
y <- rnorm(100000)
w <- rnorm(100000) - 0.1 * y
x <- rnorm(100000) + 0.1 * y
@

<<printRegs, results="asis">>=

m1 <- mcparallel(lm(y ~ x))
m2 <- mcparallel(lm(y ~ w))
texreg(list(mccollect(m1)[[1]], mccollect(m2)[[1]]))
@

\end{document}

messages.subject: Help with runtime error R6034 under windows
messages.subject_clean: Help with runtime error R6034 under windows
messages.body_plain:
Under Windows, I get a runtime error R6034 when I open any R file in gVim.  Fortunately, after I dismiss the error everything works fine!  Surely this error is not caused by the plugin, but by one of the components it uses (pywin32 is my guess).  However, I would really appreciate any help I can get in solving it.

I followed the installation instructions for Windows carefully, making sure I have the right versions of each required software.  I have:

- Vim 7.4
- R version 3.0.3
- vimcom.plus version 0.9-93
- Python 2.7.6 (32 bit)
- pywin32-218.win32-py2.7.exe
- Windows 7 pro SP1 64-bit

I searched for a solution but to no avail.  I found this:

https://code.google.com/p/vim/issues/detail?id=173

suggesting something about python loading the MSVC runtime DLL without having a correct manifest?  I don't really understand what that means.  On a different machine, also with Windows 7, it did work without this error, albeit with older versions of some of the programs (vim 7.3, python 2.7.3), so I'm not sure that my problem is related to this.

Thanks, any help appreciated!
